reviewBoundary: Three new complete junior fifteen-gap four-choice narratives. Fictional fair, paper-bridge club demonstration and postcard exchange. Same-author key and all-alternative review, shuffled choices; no independent calibration.

units.title: The bear outside the shop
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The bear outside the shop
materials.text:
I photographed the charity fair’s cake stall for our school newspaper. In the background, a huge brown bear appeared to be looking through the shop ____1____. 

I wrote, "A hungry bear visits the fair," and sent it to our student editor. She asked whether it was a real ____2____. Of course not! Our sports teacher wore a costume.

"Will everyone know that?" she asked.

The photograph did not show his trainers or the zip behind his head. Those details were outside the ____3____. A stranger might miss the joke.

We added the teacher's name to the ____4____ and explained the costume. The picture was still funny, but the joke no longer depended on a reader making a wrong ____5____.

The teacher later requested a copy. "I could hardly see through that head," he said. "I was trying to find the ____6____, not a cake."

I looked again. The bear seemed interested in the food because I had ____7____ it that way. The teacher had simply been searching for the doorway.

We printed his comment beside the image. It made the story even ____8____. Readers could laugh at a real difficulty instead of an invented appetite.

I learned to check the words I put ____9____ a picture. A photograph could contain something true while leaving out important ____10____.  I still wanted the newspaper to be ____11____. Now I also wanted a stranger to understand what had ____12____. Before the next fair, I asked the teacher whether he would wear the costume again. He said yes, provided someone helped him ____13____ the way. I volunteered, knowing the bear’s ____14____ from the ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The apparent bear looks through a shop window. Tickets, baskets and pockets are not openings in the building.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The editor asks whether the apparent bear is a real animal. A real teacher and costume already exist; photograph would ask authenticity rather than the bear’s identity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Trainers and zip are outside the photographic frame. They are physically at the fair and part of the costume’s story; shop is not the boundary of the captured view.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A caption is the explanatory text placed with a photo. Price, window and uniform do not carry the newspaper explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: A reader without context might guess incorrectly. Cake and costume are objects, journey travel, not a mistaken interpretation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The teacher was searching for the doorway, an entrance. Camera, editor and family are not the needed way into the stall.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The hungry-bear wording describes the food interest into the image. Painting, eating and breaking are not the writer’s caption action.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The actual doorway difficulty adds humour. Length, age and darkness do not name the improved comic effect.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Words are put beside a picture as its caption. Inside is not the stated accompanying text position; above all and instead are not locations for that relation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Missing trainers, zip and motive are context needed for interpretation. Prices, colours and cakes do not name the absent explanatory circumstances.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The newspaper aims to entertain with funny images. Silence, expense and privacy are not the public paper’s aim.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Readers should understand what happened. Cost, growth and disappearance are not the complete account of the fair scene.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Limited vision in costume requires help finding the way. Blocking/hiding obstruct it and forgetting does not assist.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The actual problem is finding the entrance. Colour, price and weight are not the difficulty revealed by the interview.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: From the start means the narrator understands the task beforehand. Window, cake and shop do not complete that time phrase.

units.title: The egg above the gap
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The egg above the gap
materials.text:
In science club, we were given paper, tape and an empty egg carton. We had to build a bridge to ____1____ an egg above a gap between two low tables. The teacher placed a tray underneath before we tested anything.

My group made a wide, flat bridge. It looked ____2____, but it bent as soon as we put the egg in the middle. We caught the egg before it fell and looked at the paper.

Another group had folded its sheet into several long ridges. Their bridge used no more paper than ours, yet it held the egg. I suspected extra ____3____ inside.

They showed us the bridge from every side. The difference was the ____4____, not the amount of material. We tried their folds.

The new bridge held the egg, but only if we placed it ____5____. Near an edge, the bridge twisted. We used the carton to make a small holder that kept the egg in the ____6____.

When the activity ended, the teacher asked us not to say simply that paper was weak or strong. We had seen the same material behave ____7____ when its shape changed.

I drew both bridges in my notebook. The first had failed, but keeping its picture made the ____8____ clearer. I recorded its position and the folds.

We had not built something ready for a real road. The classroom model answered a much ____9____ question.  Before throwing away a plan that seemed ____10____, I might ask what could be changed. Our strongest idea had begun with noticing another group's ____11____, not with using more tape. Sharing it did not make their work less ____12____. It helped the whole club ____13____. We tidied up and returned the egg to its ____14____. No omelette was needed to finish the ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The bridge must hold the egg above the gap. Cooking, selling and painting are not its structural task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The broad bridge looks solid but bends under load. Invisibility, emptiness and dirt do not describe apparent strength.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The supplied egg carton offers cardboard, which the narrator suspects as hidden reinforcement. Extra eggs add load, tables are supports and notebooks not the suspected concealed material.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Folding changes shape without adding paper. Colour and price are unchanged, and extra weight was not added.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Position matters, so the egg must be placed carefully. Secrecy, time and location outside do not address balance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The holder keeps the egg in the centre rather than at an edge. Air/gap leave it unsupported and no pocket is made.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The same paper works differently after folding. Equally denies the observed change; sound and speed are not the compared property.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Keeping both versions makes their comparison clear. Room, egg and tape are objects, not the explanatory relationship.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A classroom model answers a smaller question than engineering a road bridge. Loudness, age and weight do not express scope.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: An apparently failed/hopeless plan may be changed. Finished is not failure, and expense/popularity are not the initial problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: They learn another group’s folding method. Lunch, uniform and teacher identity do not supply the new design technique.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Sharing the technique does not make the work less valuable. It does reduce privacy and invisibility, while colour is unrelated to the contribution.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The shared method helps everyone learn. Sleep and leaving are unrelated; competition is not the collaborative result described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The egg returns safely to its carton. Window and pocket are unsuitable storage, while leaving it on the test bridge is not putting it back.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The club completes an experiment without breaking the egg for an omelette. A real road and breakfast are not the task; no competition is established.

units.title: The postcards that never needed stamps
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The postcards that never needed stamps
materials.text:
Our art club exchanged postcards with another school. The cards travelled in one large envelope, so individual stamps were not ____1____. I drew one anyway because I liked its appearance.

My picture showed a lane behind our sports centre. I wanted it to look ____2____, adding imaginary towers. Our teacher asked why I had chosen the place. Warm afternoon light, I explained. I removed the towers and worked on the ____3____ instead.

On the back, I asked, "What ordinary place would you show a stranger?" I did not know who would ____4____ my card.

Two weeks later, a reply arrived. It showed a laundrette, with clothes turning behind round windows. The writer waited there with her father on Sundays and liked the repeated ____5____.

I was surprised, then remembered my lane. Both places mattered because someone had spent time ____6____ them. Neither needed a famous name.

With permission, we displayed the cards. When visitors asked about the places, we showed them the words on the ____7____. The pictures began conversations rather than telling the whole story alone.

My drawn stamp had no practical ____8____. It was decoration, not a claim that the card had travelled alone. The real journey was the ____9____ between our choices. Exchanging pictures did not make the places ____10____; it made their differences interesting.

Next time, I would ask another question rather than simply send a more ____11____ picture. A reply was not a prize for drawing well. It was an ____12____ to see through another person's attention. The turning circles above my desk reminded me to look ____13____ at the familiar. A place became worth sharing when someone took the ____14____ to see it, and someone else was willing to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Cards travel together in one envelope, so stamps on each are not required. Cost, availability and colour do not express that postage rule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Imaginary castle towers are added to impress, beyond the ordinary lane. Empty/private/ancient are not the embellishment aim established by making a tourist-like view.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Afternoon light motivated choosing the lane, so the teacher redirects work to it. Price, map and stamp are not that observed attraction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The unknown exchange partner will receive the card. Selling, painting and hiding are not its destination role.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Round windows and turning clothes form repeated circles, echoed by turning circles at the end. Prices, customers and stories do not name those shapes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Attention over time makes ordinary places meaningful. Selling, avoiding and repairing are not what both writers describe doing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The question and explanation are written on the back. Wall is the depicted subject, the shared envelope not individual text and the drawn stamp decoration.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The drawn stamp serves no postal function. It visibly has colour and a maker; price/owner do not name the missing practical use.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The question and reply create a conversation between choices. Distance is physical, competition would seek a winner and schedule timing, not that exchange of perspectives.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Sharing does not make the places identical; differences become interesting. It does make their value/visibility noticeable, while fame is not the comparison intended.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The narrator chooses a better question rather than only a more beautiful image. Ordinary/local describe the current subject and private contradicts exchange; beauty is the artistic-performance measure later contrasted with conversation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The reply invites another perspective. Order commands, excuse evades and obstacle blocks, opposite the open exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Look again means reconsider the familiar with fresh attention. Away avoids it, yesterday is a time reference and alone company, not renewed looking.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Take the time to see means devote attention. Train, money and stamp do not complete this attentional phrase.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Another person willing to listen completes a shared perspective. Winning, leaving and hiding do not engage with the account.
